slidelink.displaytext: Module 5.2: Practical Application of the 5-Step CQI Process
Meet the Scenario: Unity Center, Cherry County
Which Data Point Warrants a CQI Cycle?
What Makes a Good Problem Statement?

slidetranscripts.slidetranscript:
<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Welcome to Module 5.2, the second installment in the last module of the CQI training series. In this module, we will cover the practical applications of the 5-step CQI process.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Select “Next” to begin." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The learning objectives of this module are to:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Apply California’s 5-Step CQI Process to prevention services.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Learn practical steps to integrate the 5-Step CQI Process into agency workflows.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And develop strategies to overcome common CQI implementation barriers." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Module 5 is divided into four brief applications:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 1: Review of modules 1-4 and how to interpret fidelity and outcome metrics.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 2: How to identify and define a problem from fidelity and outcome metrics and how to conduct a root cause analysis.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 3: Developing, implementing, testing, and revising solutions.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 4: Key implementation barriers and how to address them.In this session, we will be covering Brief Application 2." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Problems often show up first in data summaries and visualizations like this dashboard. Start by getting your bearings: who, what, when, and where. This data comes from the Unity Center for Family Growth and Development's Healthy Families America program in Cherry County, and covers October 1 through December 31, 2024. It includes 200 primary caregivers, 80 infants, and 260 children. Each bar shows one outcome measure as a percentage, and the " /> <Span Text="red" /> <Span Text=" line marks its target. As you look at each bar, ask yourself: how does it compare to its target?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Before we look at any data, let's set up the scenario we'll be working with for the rest of this module.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Where: the Unity Center for Family Growth and Development, in Cherry County.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Who: primary caregivers, their infants, and older children enrolled in Healthy Families America.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="When: October 1 through December 31, 2024.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And what: outcomes reported as percentages.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Those four details are what make a problem specific enough to act on. Hold onto them — you'll use every one of them when we write a problem statement later in this module." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Five outcomes metrics are tracked for this provider. Let’s review each one and its relationship to the target level. Going from " /> <Span Text="top to bottom" /> <Span Text=", the percent of primary caregivers with children in the target age range whose caregiver-child interaction was assessed using a validated too" /> <Span Text="l" /> <Span Text=" is at the target level of 90%. The percent of infants (among mothers who enrolled in home visiting prenatally before 37 weeks) who are born preterm following program enrollment is at 10% which is below the target level of 15%. The percent of children enrolled in home visiting with a timely screen for developmental delays using a validated parent-completed tool is at 89% which is just below the target level of 90%. The percent of children enrolled in home visiting referred for services for a positive screen for developmental delays (measured using a validated tool) who receive services in a timely manner is at 86% below the target of 90%. Finally, the percent of primary caregivers enrolled in home visiting for at least three months who were screened for depression within 3 months of enrollment of 3 months of delivery (for those enrolled prenatally) is at 60% and the target is 80%." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="CQI cycles can require a fair amount of work so it is best to focus on one issue at a time unless it is clear you have the resources to work on multiple issues at once. If a program is not meeting expectations in multiple areas you may need to choose which area is the most pressing. While the HFA program in this scenario is below the target level on four data points, it is within 5 points of the target for improved pregnancy outcomes and improved child health and development. This may be simply reflect normal variation in practice (the outcomes will fluctuate across reporting periods) or may be small problems that bears watching. In contrast, improved caregiver health is 20 percentage points below the target level. This is a significant gap. While it could be a one-time issue reflecting unique circumstances within the reporting period and it is always important to talk to an agency to understand the context surrounding the data, it is also likely a better candidate for a CQI cycle." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The team has chosen Improved Caregiver Health as the focus of this CQI cycle. Again this is defined as: The percent of primary caregivers enrolled in home visiting for at least three months who were screened for depression within the required timeframe. The Required Timeframe is within 3 months of enrollment, OR within 3 months of delivery for caregivers enrolled prenatally.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Now that we know what problem to investigate the next step is writing a clear problem statement." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Before you write a problem statement, it helps to know what a good one looks like. A strong problem statement names both the program and the population the data describes. It uses language that matches or closely mirrors the data point itself. When there's a target available, it describes how far off you are. And it's specific about who, what, and when.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Just as important is what a problem statement leaves out. It doesn't name a cause — that's Step 2's job, not this one. It avoids vague language like 'poor' or 'too low' or 'not high enough.' It doesn't skip the program name or the population. And it doesn't leave out the extent of the gap.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Keep these in mind as we build one from the Cherry County data." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Every strong problem statement contains five components. Let's break one down, using the details we know.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The time period for this scenario is between October 1 and December 31, 2024. The population is comprised of primary caregivers, enrolled for at least three months. This is within the Unity Center for Family Growth and Development's Healthy Families America program. Our metric is the percentage of individuals screened for depression within the required timeframe. And finally, the extent of our gap was 20 points below the target level." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Here are three examples of problem statements that miss the mark — and what to fix.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Example 1: Depression screenings are poor at Unity Center. This statement is missing the program name, population, time period, and extent of gap. The use of 'poor' is vague and should be more descriptive.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Example 2: Caregivers aren't being screened because staff don't have training. This statement lists a cause, however, causes belong in Step 2 instead of the problem statement.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Example 3: The depression screening rate is not high enough. The statement is vague when stating the rate is "not high enough." You should quantify the gap, such as "20 percentage points below target."" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Now we have our problem statement: Between October 1 and December 31, 2024, the percentage of primary caregivers enrolled for at least three months in the Unity Center's HFA program who were screened for depression within the required timeframe was 20 percentage points below the target level.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="We will now move to Step 2 of the CQI Cycle: Understand the Underlying Conditions, using the 5 Whys of Root Cause Analysis." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The 5 Whys is a root cause analysis technique. By asking why again and again, a team moves past the surface symptoms to the underlying cause. It’s not the only option. You may have used a fishbone diagram or another method, and that’s fine. What matters is having a structured way to dig past the symptoms.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The 5 Whys is about as simple as it gets. Start with the problem and ask, “Why is this happening?” Then take that answer and ask why again. Keep going until you reach a cause you can actually act on. Five rounds is a guideline, not a limit. It usually takes at least five to get past the surface, and sometimes more.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let’s put it into practice with the problem we defined in Part 1. Depression screening at Unity Center is 20 percentage points below target. That’s where we’ll start asking why." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Why 1 of 5: Why aren’t depression screenings being done?Answer: HFA caseworkers are not consistently completing the PHQ-9 or EPDS screening tool with caregivers during home visits. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="This is our initial contributing cause. But why is this happening? Move onto the next “Why” to learn more." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Why 4 of 5: Why are caseworkers unsure how to raise the subject?Answer: Caseworkers have not received training or practice on how to introduce depression screening in a trauma-informed, supportive way.Lack of training leads to lack of confidence. One more “Why” may take us to the root cause." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Now we have completed the “5 Whys Method” and identified the root cause. The Cherry County Local CQI Team has determined that the HFA caseworkers are not consistently screening caregivers for depression using the PHQ-9 or EPDS because they feel uncomfortable asking about depression.In the following section, we will take a knowledge check and have a brief look at what comes next." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#262626" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Congratulations! You’ve completed Brief Application 2 of Module 5. Let’s check our learning before moving on.Select the button below to start." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Question #1, What is the purpose of the 5 Whys technique?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 1: To write the problem statement,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 2: To keep asking ‘why’ until the team reaches the root cause of a problem,
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 3: To identify all possible solutions to a problem." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Question #2, In Cherry County's 5 Whys, what is the root cause?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 1: Caseworkers do not have enough time during home visits.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 2: The PHQ-9 and EPDS screening tools are too difficult to administer.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="36" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Option 3: Caseworkers feel uncomfortable asking caregivers about depression." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>
